papers.title: Threshold Attainment and Sharp Asymptotics for $L^p$-Perturbed Moser--Trudinger Functionals on $\mathbb{R}^2$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the critical Moser--Trudinger supremum \[ S(\lambda,p) = \sup_{\substack{ u\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^2)\\ \int_{\mathbb{R}^2} (|\nabla u|^2+u^2)\,dx\le 1 }} \int_{\mathbb{R}^2} \left(e^{4\pi u^2}-1-\lambda |u|^p\right)\,dx, \qquad p\ge 2. \] Building on the classification away from the thresholds by Chen, Jiang, Lu and Zhu (2026), we resolve the endpoint cases: both thresholds for $p=2$ and the finite threshold for $2<p\le4$ are attained. We also prove compactness of centred radial extremals and one-sided value expansions governed by the selected endpoint $L^p$ mass. For $p>4$, we quantify how extremals spread out as $\lambda\to\infty$ by establishing the two-term expansion \[ S(\lambda,p)=4\pi+\mathcal C_p\lambda^{-2/(p-4)} +D_p\lambda^{-4/(p-4)}+o\bigl(\lambda^{-4/(p-4)}\bigr), \] Here $\mathcal C_p$ is the maximum of a limiting variational problem at unit $L^2$ mass. An explicit correction involving the sixth moment and the full $H^1$ normalization determines $D_p$ and selects the limiting maximizers. Rescaled centred radial extremals converge strongly to these profiles in $H^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$ along subsequences. For every fixed $\lambda>\lambda_*(4)$, we further establish \[ \lim_{p\downarrow4}(p-4)\log\bigl(S(\lambda,p)-4\pi\bigr) =2\log\frac{\lambda_{\mathrm{loc}}}{\lambda}<0, \] where $\lambda_{\mathrm{loc}}$ is the local critical penalty determined by the sharp Gagliardo--Nirenberg constant. The gradient energy has the same logarithmic rate, and the centred radial profiles, normalized in mass and gradient energy, converge along subsequences to sharp Gagliardo--Nirenberg optimizers. An exact transfer identity extends these endpoint and asymptotic results to every constant planar norm.

papers.title: Ergodicity for stochastic neural field equations
papers.abstract: We investigate the well-posedness and long-time behavior of a general continuum neural field model with Gaussian noise on possibly unbounded domains. In particular, we give conditions for the existence of invariant probability measures by restricting the solution flow to an invariant subspace with a nonlocal metric. Under the assumption of a sufficiently large decay parameter relative to the noise intensity, the norm of the connectivity kernel operator, and the Lipschitz regularity of the activation function, we establish exponential ergodicity and exponential mixing of the associated Markovian Feller semigroup and the uniqueness of the invariant measure.

papers.title: A Sharp Planar Fractional Isoperimetric Inequality
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove the sharp form of the fractional isoperimetric inequality in the plane, originally posed by Maz'ya [Problem 1, Integral Equations Operator Theory, 2018]. More precisely, we show that, for any given $s\in(0,1)$ and any bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with $C^1$ boundary, $$ P_s(\Omega) \le \frac{\pi^{s-\frac{1}{2}}\Gamma\left(\frac{3-s}{2}\right)}{s(1-s)\Gamma\left(\frac{4-s}{2}\right)}\left[\mathcal{H}^1(\partial\Omega)\right]^{2-s}, $$ where $P_s$ denotes the fractional $s$-perimeter, $\Gamma$ denotes the Gamma function, and $\mathcal{H}^{1}$ denotes the $1$-dimensional Hausdorff measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$. The constant is sharp and equality is attained by the disk. The proof proceeds in three steps: reducing the fractional perimeter to a chord functional, reducing connected domains to convex bodies, and proving the sharp convex chord inequality via a fractional Willmore-type inequality, a variational formula along outer parallel bodies, and asymptotic analysis.

papers.title: Kirszbraun's Intersection Property and Nonexpansive Extensions
papers.abstract: This paper aims to present the historical development of the extension problem of nonexpansive maps in Euclidean and Hilbert spaces, and to serve as a comprehensive guide to this specific area. Such extensions are based on a geometric property of the intersection of closed balls in Euclidean spaces, known as the Kirszbraun intersection property. Subsequently, a number of authors have extended this property to Hilbert and other spaces. All these results are discussed in this paper, but the paper itself is not a mechanical compilation of already known proofs. The material has been developed with an emphasis on the natural connections between all these results and the corresponding concepts involved in them. Furthermore, most of these results are presented with new simplified proofs. Last but not least, the paper also contains some new results related to this extension problem.

papers.title: New matrix-weighted norm inequalities and extrapolation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a new type of matrix-weighted theory and show the corresponding Rubio de Francia extrapolation theorems by means of noncommutative maximal inequalities. We introduce a new matrix $A_p$ condition following Volberg's geometric formulation, and characterize it via a noncommutative Hardy--Littlewood maximal inequality. We then establish a noncommutative analogue of Rubio de Francia's abstract extrapolation theorem for trace-finite von Neumann algebras. The argument extends to $L_\infty(\mathbb R)\bar\otimes M_d(\mathbb C)$ through pointwise matrix operations. This yields the desired extrapolation results for individual operators and maximal families, with applications to matrix-weighted boundedness of Calder\'on--Zygmund operators.

papers.title: On the existence of independent inner functions
papers.abstract: The existence of independent inner functions is established: there exist inner functions $\varphi$ and $\psi$, both vanishing at the origin, such that $$ \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} \varphi^m(e^{i\theta}) \overline{\psi^n(e^{i\theta})}\,d\theta = 0, \qquad m,n \geq 1. $$ In fact, both $\varphi$ and $\psi$ can be chosen to be Blaschke products. The proof proceeds by an iterative construction, which suggests a general approach to produce inner functions with a desired joint distribution.

papers.title: On Continuous Wavelet Transform of Complex Radon Measures on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$
papers.abstract: This paper investigates a necessary and sufficient condition for a measurable function on $\mathbb{R}^{\times} \times \mathbb{R}^{d}$ to be the continuous wavelet transform of a complex Radon measure on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ under suitable regularity conditions on the wavelets. We define a new norm on the collection of such functions and show that it is isometrically isomorphic to the Banach algebra of complex Radon measures under convolution. We show a wavelet inversion formula for measures, in a restricted sense. Under additional hypothesis, we provide a reconstruction formula for the measure of closed rectangles in $\mathbb{R}^d$ using wavelet transforms. We have included supporting examples to substantiate these assumptions.

papers.title: Cyclic group tensors and the volume ratio of projective tensor products
papers.abstract: We revisit the problem of estimating the norm of the natural embedding from the Euclidean space $\ell_2^{n^3}$ into the projective tensor product $\ell_p^n\otimes_\pi\ell_q^n\otimes_\pi\ell_r^n$ in the range $1\le p\le q\le 2\le r\le\infty$, studied by Giladi, Prochno, Sch\"utt, Tomczak-Jaegermann and Werner [J. Funct. Anal. 273 (2017), 471-495]. Using convolution on finite cyclic groups, we establish new lower bounds that improve their estimates and determine the exact asymptotic order of the embedding norm whenever $1/p+1/q+1/r\ge 2$. We then apply an estimate of Boedihardjo for the injective norm of random tensors to a randomly signed cyclic convolution tensor and use multilinear interpolation to determine the optimal exponent throughout the entire parameter range, up to logarithmic factors. As consequences, we obtain corresponding improvements and asymptotically sharp estimates, up to logarithmic factors, for the volume ratio of these projective tensor products.

papers.title: Numerical Shadow Rigidity for 3x3 Matrices
papers.abstract: The numerical shadow of a complex matrix is the measure obtained by pushing forward that Haar measure on the unit sphere in $\mathbb{C}^n$ by the numerical range map. By the choice of measure, unitary equivalence implies same measure, but the reverse is not true for $n\geq 3$. We name a matrix $\textbf{shadow rigid}$ it its unitary equivalence class and shadow equivalence class coincide. It is known that normal matrices are rigid, but the topic has not been explored beyond this in the literature. The main result of the paper is showing that in the $n=3$ case, a matrix is rigid if and only if it is non-generic. We also show that rigidity is preserved under an affine group action and present three normal-like properties of $3\times 3$ non-generic matrices.

papers.title: Weighted composition operators on the Fock space
papers.abstract: In this paper, we discuss the compactness, invertibility and isometry of the operators on the Fock space formed by multiplying a weighted composition operator with the adjoint of another weighted composition operator to form either $W_{g, \psi}W_{f, \varphi}^*$ or $W_{g, \psi}^*W_{f, \varphi}$.

papers.title: Duality in Harmonic Analysis and beyond
papers.abstract: In this short note, we develop a duality-based, purely operator-theoretic method for proving several classical maximal inequalities on $L^p$ spaces for $p\in(1,\infty)$. The method applies to maximal ergodic operators, Hardy--Littlewood maximal functions, and maximal Radon averaging operators, and derives their boundedness directly from structural properties of the underlying operators. Further, we show that the same duality principle extends beyond maximal functions. We develop a theory of $r$-variational and jump inequalities for sequences of bounded positive monotone operators on Hilbert spaces, using soft arguments that apply to various classical operators in analysis. In particular, answering a question that had been open for some time, we give direct proofs of $r$-variational and jump inequalities for convolution operators associated with lacunary dilations of smooth bumps on $\mathbb R^d$, completely avoiding any appeal to martingale inequalities.

papers.title: Numerical Information of Hilbert Space Operators
papers.abstract: For a Hilbert space operator $A\in B(H)$, the numerical range map of $A$, denoted $\phi_A$ is the map sending unit vectors $x$ in $H$ to $\langle Ax,x\rangle$. From this map we define the Numerical Information of $A$, denoted $\Sigma_A$, which is the sigma algebra induced on the unit sphere by the numerical range map. One of the main results of the paper are that if $A,B\in B(H)$, and $\phi_B=f\circ \phi_A$, then $f$ is affine. Our other main result is showing that $\Sigma_B\subset\Sigma_A$ if and only if $B=\alpha Re(A)+\beta Im(A)+\gamma I$ for some complex numbers $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$.

papers.title: Explicit finite size corrections for Toeplitz determinants and rectangular domino tilings
papers.abstract: Finite Toeplitz truncation does not, in general, preserve multiplication. For products of $m$ $N\times N$ tridiagonal Toeplitz matrices with symbols $z+z^{-1}+a_h$, we make the two boundary corrections in Widom's product formula for finite sections explicit. The method of images gives two Hankel corrections when $m\le N+2$, a sharp uniform degree bound. For $N\ge m-1$, the ratio of the determinant of the matrix product to the Toeplitz determinant with the product symbol reduces, whenever defined, to a determinant of order $2(m-1)$, which reversal symmetry splits into two determinants of order $m-1$. A rectangular Schur polynomial gives an exact formula for the Toeplitz determinant with the product symbol, including when roots coincide. For symbols nonzero on the unit circle, classical identities for rational symbols give an exact $m\times m$ determinant formula for the ratio, with an explicit confluent form for repeated roots. With $\rho_h$ the zero of $z+z^{-1}+a_h$ in $|z|<1$, the limit is $\prod_{i<j}(1-\rho_i\rho_j)^2$ as $N\to\infty$ at fixed $m,a_h$. For rectangular domino tilings, these formulas compare the classical Kasteleyn--Temperley--Fisher product with the banded Toeplitz determinant formed from the product symbol. We obtain the first exponentially small correction at fixed width and relate this comparison to the Toeplitz determinant furnished by the dual Cauchy identity.

papers.title: Rudin's Problem on Uniformly Bounded Homogeneous Orthonormal Bases
papers.abstract: Rudin's problem asks whether, in the unit ball of $\mathbb C^d$ with $d\ge2$ fixed, the Hardy space $H^2(\partial\mathbb B_d)$ admits a uniformly bounded orthonormal basis consisting of homogeneous holomorphic polynomials. For $d=2$ and $d=3$ the answer is due to Bourgain, but the general-dimensional case has remained open. This paper gives an affirmative answer to Rudin's problem in every fixed dimension. More precisely, we prove that there is an orthonormal basis consisting of homogeneous polynomials $\{p_j\}_{j=1}^\infty$ of $H^2(\partial\mathbb B_d)$ such that $$\|p_j\|_{L^\infty(\partial\mathbb B_d)}\leq \exp\left(\frac12d\log d+O(d)\right).$$ Here the implicit constant in $O(d)$ is independent of $d$ and $j$.

papers.title: Irregular Gabor Frames for the Poisson Kernel
papers.abstract: Consider the semi-regular system of time-frequency shifts of the Poisson kernel $g(t) = {{1} \over {t^2+w^2}}$ $$\G(g, M \times \alpha \Z) = \left\{ e^{2\pi i \lambda t } g(t-n) \colon (\lambda, n) \in M \times \alpha\Z \right\}$$ where $M \subset \R$. We obtain {\it a criterion} for $\G(g, M \times \alpha \Z)$ to form a frame in $L^2(\R)$ for an {\it arbitrary} set $M$ of finite upper density. It turned out that the lower density alone does not determine the frame property, even when $M$ is uniformly discrete.

papers.title: Widom asymptotics for spatial compressions of Schr\"odinger spectral projections
papers.abstract: We establish a Widom trace formula for spatial compressions of exact spectral projections of semiclassical Schr\"odinger operators. The potential is smooth near a compact classically allowed region, and the observation domain lies strictly inside that region. For every continuous spectral function with positive power decay at both endpoints, we obtain a trace formula at scale $h^{1-n}\log h^{-1}$ whose coefficient separates into a boundary integral and a universal spectral functional. This yields the exact von Neumann and R\'enyi entanglement asymptotics for every fixed positive order, and proves their universal ratios to the particle-number variance. The proof combines commutator estimates in every fixed positive Schatten class with a local trace formula obtained from a boundary-adapted normal form and a Hardy model. In dimensions $n\ge2$, a positive partition and the known variance asymptotic control the grazing contribution; in one dimension all boundary Fermi points are transverse. A harmonic-oscillator counterexample shows that continuity and weighted integrability alone are insufficient for the trace formula.

papers.title: Unitary similarity for dual complex matrices and dual quaternion matrices
papers.abstract: We study unitary similarity of dual complex matrices and dual quaternion matrices. First, we characterize unitary similarity in terms of the existence of a skew-Hermitian solution to a Sylvester-type matrix equation. For $2\times2$ dual complex matrices, we obtain a complete three-trace criterion when the standard part is nonnormal and analyze the limitations of trace-word criteria when the standard part is normal. We then prove, for every $n\geq1$, that two $n\times n$ dual quaternion matrices are unitarily similar if and only if their dual complex adjoint matrices are unitarily similar, and we extend this result to finite families. As a scalar consequence, we derive a finite Trace-word criterion when the standard part is nonreal and exhibit its failure when the standard part is real.

papers.title: Joint Uniform Continuity of Reduced Free Products for strong convergence
papers.abstract: We investigate a generalization of Skoufranis' theorem on joint continuity of free products of laws in the strong topology. Namely, we show that this operation is moreover \emph{uniformly continuous}. Our methods follows those of Piser and go through the estimates of Ricard-Xu.

papers.title: Gaussian Processes with Sample Paths in Reproducing Kernel Banach Spaces
papers.abstract: We investigate the connection between Gaussian processes and Gaussian random elements in reproducing kernel Banach spaces. We show that the covariance operator of a weak second-order Radon probability measure on such a space is uniquely determined by a symmetric positive-definite function. In the Gaussian case, we characterize those functions that arise from covariance operators in terms of $\gamma$-radonifying operators. Building on these results, we extend Driscoll's theorem to the reproducing kernel Banach space setting.

papers.title: Classification of bipartite observables II: NIP observables and the Todorcevic trichotomy
papers.abstract: This is the second of a series of three papers that bring model theory to quantum information. The dividing lines of Shelah's classification theory, which separate the tame first-order theories from the wild ones, become properties of bipartite observables: properties of the expectation values obtained when two independently prepared quantum systems are idealized one after the other. In this paper we focus on Shelah's independence property. An observable without it has idealized responses of the first Baire class, and Todor\v{c}evi\'c's trichotomy for Rosenthal compacta divides such observables into three classes, each containing a physical order. In the transverse-field Ising model, the spontaneous magnetization decides whether the family of magnetizations is stable or lies in the second class.

papers.title: Cwikel estimates and Weyl's laws for $L\log L$ potentials on quantum tori
papers.abstract: We prove an $L\log L$-endpoint Cwikel estimate on quantum tori $\mathbb T_\theta^d$, i.e., for every $d\geq 2$ and $x\in L\log L(\mathbb T_\theta^d)$, \begin{equation*} \big\|(1-\Delta)^{-\frac{d}{4}}\lambda(x)(1-\Delta)^{-\frac{d}{4}}\big\|_{\mathcal{L}_{1,\infty}} \leq C_d \Norm{x}_{L\log L(\mathbb T_\theta^d)}, \end{equation*} where $\lambda(x)$ is the left multiplication by $x$. Our argument actually gives an abstract weak Hilbert--Schmidt estimate for multiplication operators in finite von Neumann algebras whose $L_2$-spaces admit orthonormal bases of unitaries. As a consequence, it yields a critical Sobolev embedding $W_2^{d/2}\hookrightarrow\exp(L_2)$ on quantum tori. When $\theta=0$, our method also gives a simpler proof of the $L\log L$ Cwikel estimate on classical tori. As an application, we use the $C^*$-algebraic principal symbol map to prove Weyl's laws for sandwich operators \[ S(1-\Delta)^{-d/4}\lambda(x)(1-\Delta)^{-d/4}T, \] where $x\in L\log L(\mathbb T_\theta^d)$ and $S,T\in\Pi$, the $C^*$-algebra generated by $\lambda(C(\mathbb T_\theta^d))$ and Fourier multipliers with continuous homogeneous symbols of degree zero. We also prove a semiclassical Weyl's law for critical Schr\"odinger operators with $L\log L$ potentials.

papers.title: A survey of sampling discretization of integral and uniform norms
papers.abstract: This paper surveys recent developments in the sampling discretization of integral and uniform norms for functions in general finite-dimensional spaces. These results generalize the classical Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund inequalities for trigonometric and algebraic polynomials, which play a crucial role in Fourier analysis, interpolation, and approximation theory. We focus on the problem in the broad context of finite-dimensional subspaces, where norms defined by general probability measures are approximated by their discrete counterparts. The primary emphasis is on results closely related to the authors' recent research. A key objective is to highlight the main ideas and techniques that form the foundation of the proofs in this area. This survey serves as a complement to three recently published survey papers on sampling discretization \cite{DPTT, KKLT, LMT}.

papers.title: Hardy-Sobolev-Maz'ya inequalities for $\boldsymbol{1<p<2}$
papers.abstract: We establish Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequalities in the subquadratic range $1<p<2$ for singularities supported on affine subspaces and for arbitrary domains. We first prove a Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequality for singularities supported on affine subspaces of arbitrary codimension $1\leq k<N$, showing that the deficit in the sharp Hardy inequality controls a suitable weighted Sobolev norm. Combining the same convexity estimate with the one-dimensional approach of Frank and Loss in [9], we also establish Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequalities on arbitrary domains with the mean distance to the boundary and thereby solve a problem posed in [9]. These results complete the previously unresolved subquadratic range $1<p<2$ and, together with the known results for $p\geq 2$, provide a unified Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya theory for all $1<p<N$ associated with plane singularities and general domains.

papers.title: Maximal Plurisubharmonic Functions and Fujii-Seo Determinants in Hilbert spaces
papers.abstract: A maximal plurisubharmonic function on an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space can have an injective, noncompact Levi operator at every point. This raises the question of what replaces the finite-dimensional determinant criterion for maximality. We prove that a twice continuously differentiable plurisubharmonic function is maximal if its Levi operator is compact at every point, without any boundedness assumption on the function. Using the normalized determinants of Fujii and Seo, we also characterize local maximality by the condition that the infimum of the spectrum of the Levi operator is zero. The same condition characterizes maximality when the function is bounded on the closure of every bounded open set whose closure lies in the domain. The compactness result follows from a more general spectral criterion. Its proof combines a bounded transformation with the smooth variational principle of Borwein and Preiss to establish comparison on bounded open sets whose closures need not be compact.

papers.title: Non-symmetric vector dyson equations
papers.abstract: We study the vector Dyson equation $$-\frac{1}{m(z)}=z\mathbf{1}-\mathbf{a}+Sm(z),$$ with parameter $z$ in the complex upper half-plane $\mathbb{C}_+$, where $\mathbf{a}\in\mathbb R^d$ and $S$ is a nonnegative matrix, not necessarily symmetric. This equation has a unique vector solution $m(z)\in\mathbb{C}_+^d$, for which we establish a complete measure decomposition and prove regularity. We then develop a graph-theoretic approach to the singularity and stability problem for non-symmetric matrices $S$. The graph structure of $S$ identifies the possible degeneracies of the stability operator as $z$ approaches the real axis. In particular, for non-backtracking matrices, we prove square-root growth at regular edges, cubic-root growth at regular cusps, and complete stability estimates. We also obtain the corresponding estimates for symmetric matrices in the periodic setting.

papers.title: Complete Self-Shrinkers in Arbitrary Codimension with Positive Constant Scalar Curvature and $S\le 1$
papers.abstract: Let \(X:M^n\to\mathbb R^{n+p}\) be an \(n\)-dimensional complete self-shrinker in arbitrary codimension \(p\ge 1\). Suppose that the scalar curvature \(R\) is a positive constant and that the squared norm \(S\) of the second fundamental form satisfies \(S\le 1\). We prove that \(S\equiv 1\) and that \(X\) is isometric to either the round sphere \(S^n(\sqrt n)\) or the standard generalized cylinder \(S^k(\sqrt k)\times\mathbb R^{n-k}\), \(2\le k\le n-1\). In particular, no new higher-codimension examples occur under these assumptions. The proof uses an algebraic lemma which yields a uniform positive lower bound for the Bakry--\'Emery Ricci curvature, together with the comparison theorem of Wei--Wylie, the equivalence of finite Gaussian volume and polynomial volume growth due to Cheng--Zhou, and the gap theorem of Cao--Li.

papers.title: Norms of the Hilbert Matrix Operator on Some Analytic Function Spaces
papers.abstract: For $\mathcal H:\mathcal B^\alpha\to\mathcal B^\alpha$ with $1<\alpha<2$, we obtain an exact norm representation. In particular, the norm is given by an explicit Gamma-function formula for $1<\alpha\leq3/2$, whereas for $3/2<\alpha<2$ it strictly exceeds the corresponding Gamma-function expression. For $\mathcal H:\mathcal B^\alpha\to\mathcal B^\alpha_{\log}$, we determine the exact norm: it is equal to $3/2$ for $1<\alpha\leq4/3$ and is given by an explicit Gamma-function formula for $4/3<\alpha<2$. We also determine the exact norm of $\mathcal H:H^1\to H^1_{\log}$ and show that it is equal to $\pi$. Finally, for $0<\alpha<1$, we determine the exact norm of $\mathcal H:H^\infty_\alpha\to\mathcal B^{\alpha+1}$, which is given by an explicit Gamma-function formula.

papers.title: Second quantization and compactness of induced Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups
papers.abstract: We characterize compactness of the Hilbert-Schmidt semigroups induced by finite-mode Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups with a faithful normal invariant state. A unitary second-quantization representation for every $ s $-embedding shows that compactness at one positive time, compact resolvent, drift stability, and uniqueness of the normal invariant state are equivalent. These conditions imply immediate trace-class membership for all embeddings. We derive exact trace-norm and Hilbert-Schmidt norm formulas, an embedding-independent trace identity, and the generator spectrum with algebraic multiplicities. Examples show that compactness does not require the existence of a spectral gap and that a spectral gap need not imply compactness when the invariant state is not unique.
